name: Conductive Deafness-Malformed External Ear Syndrome
aliases: Congenital Conductive Hearing Loss with External Ear Malformation
External Ear Dysplasia with Conductive Hearing Impairment

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Conductive Deafness-Malformed External Ear Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital malformation of the external ear including microtia or anotia
Confirmed conductive hearing loss demonstrated by audiometric testing
Imaging evidence of malformed or absent middle ear ossicles
Preserved cochlear function on otoacoustic emissions or auditory brainstem response
Positive family history of similar external ear malformations and hearing loss

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital external ear malformation plus confirmed conductive hearing loss with imaging evidence of middle ear ossicular abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies on clinical, audiometric, and imaging findings; genetic testing may be supportive but is not definitive.

common.symptomName: Abnormality of the middle ear ossicles

occasional.symptomName: Stenosis of the external auditory canal

laboratory: Normal otoacoustic emissions indicating preserved cochlear function
imaging: CT or MRI demonstrating malformed or absent ossicles and external auditory canal abnormalities
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible familial inheritance patterns reported
other: Audiometric testing confirming conductive hearing loss

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of external auditory canal without ossicular malformation
Usually isolated without external ear malformation
Presence of craniofacial dysmorphisms beyond ear malformations
Bilateral symmetrical ear anomalies with mandibulofacial dysostosis

redFlags: Progressive worsening of hearing loss beyond conductive component
Presence of associated craniofacial or neurological abnormalities
references: Orphanet: Conductive Deafness-Malformed External Ear Syndrome (ORPHA:3216)
Smith RJH, et al. Congenital Conductive Hearing Loss. In: GeneReviews. 2020.
Jackler RK, et al. The External Ear and Conductive Hearing Loss. Otolaryngol Clin North Am. 2018.
